summary: This method handles downloading a file by validating the filename, checking that the file exists, setting appropriate HTTP headers to trigger a browser download, and then reading the file contents to the client. It's the server-side logic that makes a file available for download when a user clicks a download button.

explanations.9: The filename is cleaned up by removing whitespace and running it through a sanitization function to prevent directory traversal attacks or other malicious input.
explanations.11: After trimming and sanitizing, if the filename is empty, it means the user didn't actually specify a real file, so we throw an error.
explanations.15: This checks if the file actually exists in the output folder before we try to send it; if it doesn't exist, we throw an error instead of crashing.
explanations.20: We build the complete file path by combining the output folder with the filename, using ltrim to remove any leading slashes the user might have included.
explanations.22: We extract just the file extension (like 'pdf' or 'docx') from the full path so we can tell the browser what type of file this is.
explanations.24: We look up the correct MIME type (like 'application/pdf') based on the file extension so the browser knows how to handle it.
explanations.26: HTTP headers tell the browser how to treat the data we're about to send; this one says 'this is a PDF' or 'this is a Word document', etc.
explanations.27: This header tells the browser the file is being transferred as binary data, not text.
explanations.29: This header is the key one for downloads — it tells the browser 'treat this as an attachment to save to disk' rather than displaying it, and provides the filename to suggest.
explanations.30: We tell the browser how many bytes of data to expect so it can show an accurate progress bar.
explanations.35: This clears PHP's output buffer to make sure nothing else gets sent before our file data.
explanations.37: The @ suppresses any error warnings, and readfile sends the actual file contents to the browser so it gets downloaded.
